verdict: ROAS surged this week, but purchase volume stays thin and uneven.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, your Meta ads returned $5.98 for every $1 spent — and that return-on-ad-spend figure jumped 56% in the most recent week versus the week prior, while spend actually pulled back 9%, meaning the efficiency gain came from better targeting, not more budget. That said, only 35 purchases occurred across the full 28-day window, and the revenue is lumpy: a single day (August 11) accounts for a disproportionate share, so the strong ROAS number reflects a concentrated spike rather than a broad, steady sales pattern. Your Google Business Profile engagement dropped sharply this past week, and we're investigating to make sure local search visibility stays active alongside paid. The live-cooking shoot on August 14 will produce fresh content to support both ads and organic, and funnel tracking improvements are on track for end of month — both moves are aimed at building a more consistent purchase flow heading into September.

purchases recorded this period — improving but still a thin base

watch_item.issue: Purchase volume is concentrated in single-day spikes rather than spread evenly — the August 11 revenue figure is being cross-checked to confirm it reflects actual orders.
watch_item.fix: Funnel tracking is being tightened and UTM tagging goes live by end of August so every purchase is reliably attributed and we can identify which days and campaigns are truly driving conversions.
